title: Turning Torso
blurb: Santiago Calatrava’s 190 m twisting residential tower in Malmo, completed 2005: nine five-storey pentagonal cubes rotated 90 degrees around a concrete core, braced by a white steel exoskeleton.

systems.name: Foundation
systems.description: Cylindrical foundation box 30 m across and 15 m deep, on a 7 m slab piled into limestone bedrock.

systems.name: Concrete core
systems.description: The load-bearing concrete pipe: 10.6 m inner diameter, walls 2.5 m thick at the base tapering to 0.4 m at the top, carrying lifts and stairs.

systems.name: Twisting cubes
systems.description: Nine five-storey pentagonal box units, each rotated a little further, for a total twist of 90 degrees from base to top.

systems.name: Floor slabs
systems.description: Pie-slice floor slabs anchored in the concrete core, rotating with the twist.

systems.name: Aluminum facade
systems.description: Curved aluminum panels with window bands that lean in or out to follow the twist.

systems.name: Steel exoskeleton
systems.description: Tapered white steel tubes on the front face: spine columns, ring beams and diagonals that brace the tower against wind.

systems.name: Crown floors
systems.description: Observation deck, club, restaurant and conference floors at the top of the tower.

systems.name: Podium and plaza
systems.description: Entrance canopy, lobby and the plaza around the tower base.
